blocks.body:
# Commerce Labs: Load-Test Results

Three controlled local experiments ask what each mechanism protects, what changed, and what the protection costs. Values are medians of three independent run-level measurements unless stated otherwise.

## Technical summary

Cache locking reduced duplicate origin work. The transactional outbox changed broker-failure semantics, while its short normal-path latency sample remained mixed. The waiting room converted immediate rejection into FIFO queueing, preserving a four-task active cap at the cost of seconds of wait and far more polling traffic. None of these local results is a production capacity claim.

## Cache stampede

At 20→250 RPS with a 500ms TTL and controlled 40ms origin delay, both strategies completed roughly 13,850 requests per run with no dropped iterations. Origin executions, rather than hit ratio alone, are the primary protection metric.

### Interpretation

The 87.9% origin-load reduction supports the stampede-protection hypothesis. p95 improved 42.7%, but p99 improved only 1.7% and protected max-latency median rose 13.0%. Waiters still pay the refill boundary, so DB protection is not a guarantee that every latency tail improves. Redis-down and lock-timeout checks returned 503 without an unprotected DB fallback.

## Kafka direct publish vs transactional outbox

Each normal run created 97 orders at 1→2 RPS, with zero drops and final created=published=processed. The run order was fixed and low load, so percentile differences describe this sample rather than a universal speed ranking.

### Interpretation

Direct publish returned 503 after 5.021s and rolled back the order, yet an event without a matching order appeared after broker restart. Attribution to that failed request is a strong inference because its response lacked a correlation ID. Outbox returned 201 in 9.328ms, retained one pending row, and published it 14.576s after occurrence. Two relay redeliveries became one side effect through the unique event ID. The 14.576s value is occurrence-to-publish recovery time, not consumer end-to-end latency.

## Redis waiting room

Direct and queued modes received the same 10→100 iterations/s arrival profile. The queue admits only the polling FIFO head when one of four downstream slots is available. Direct used 200/1,000 preallocated/max VUs and queued used 3,000/4,000, so client resource settings were not identical even though arrival exposure was.

### Interpretation

Acceptance rose from 72.7357% to 100% while maxActive stayed at four and FIFO violations stayed at zero. This is deferred work, not 37.5% more capacity: queued accepted-flow p50/p95 were 14.055s/27.881s, median HTTP calls grew 24.022×, and backlog drain extended wall time about 23.1s. Worst wait reached 28.272s, only 1.728s below the 30s ticket TTL. Individual HTTP latency thresholds passed, but user-flow E2E latency is not currently thresholded.

## Scope and method

Runs were captured on one Apple M4 macOS host with Docker/OrbStack, Java 21, k6 0.56.0, one backend, one MySQL, one Redis, and one Kafka broker. Every comparison resets fixtures and counters, captures environment, preserves k6 handleSummary JSON, and stores final backend counters. Group headlines are medians of three run-level values; raw requests are not pooled.

## Limitations and robustness

These are short local mechanism tests, not production SLA or capacity evidence. CPU, GC, DB lock waits, Redis command latency, and Kafka lag were not captured as aligned time series. Cache and Kafka strategy order was fixed. Waiting-room preflights at earlier commits were interrupted or incomplete and are retained as diagnostic evidence but excluded from final comparisons. Aggregate FIFO counters were reconciled, but there is no admission event log for an independent sequence replay.

## Recommended next steps

1. Repeat on a fixed CI load host and establish regression thresholds.
2. Add aligned Prometheus resource and dependency time series.
3. Exercise multi-backend cache locks and Redis failover.
4. Test multi-relay outbox claims, backoff, poison events, and ack-after-crash.
5. Compare SSE or long polling with the current waiting-room poll amplification.
6. Connect the queue to a real stock-concurrency command.

query.description: Reproduces the three reader-facing lab summary rows from independently reconciled run medians.
query.sql: SELECT 1 AS display_order, 'Cache stampede' AS lab, 'Origin loads 985 to 119 (-87.9%)' AS observed_effect UNION ALL SELECT 2, 'Kafka outbox', 'Broker-down intent remained pending and recovered' UNION ALL SELECT 3, 'Redis waiting room', 'Acceptance 72.736% to 100%; max active 4'

query.description: Reproduces cache headline medians independently reconciled from three raw k6 summaries and backend counters per strategy.
query.sql: SELECT 'Naive' AS strategy, 'origin_loads' AS metric, 985.0 AS value UNION ALL SELECT 'Protected', 'origin_loads', 119.0 UNION ALL SELECT 'Naive', 'p50_ms', 1.213 UNION ALL SELECT 'Protected', 'p50_ms', 1.240 UNION ALL SELECT 'Naive', 'p95_ms', 42.3191 UNION ALL SELECT 'Protected', 'p95_ms', 24.2652 UNION ALL SELECT 'Naive', 'p99_ms', 46.13255 UNION ALL SELECT 'Protected', 'p99_ms', 45.36952

query.description: Reproduces Kafka normal-path latency medians from three raw k6 summaries per strategy.
query.sql: SELECT 'Direct' AS strategy, 'p50_ms' AS metric, 21.782 AS value UNION ALL SELECT 'Outbox', 'p50_ms', 17.314 UNION ALL SELECT 'Direct', 'p95_ms', 26.7258 UNION ALL SELECT 'Outbox', 'p95_ms', 23.9956 UNION ALL SELECT 'Direct', 'p99_ms', 28.47972 UNION ALL SELECT 'Outbox', 'p99_ms', 33.23932

query.description: Reproduces the two broker-interruption outcome rows from captured HTTP metadata, DB counts, and recovery counters.
query.sql: SELECT 1 AS display_order, 'Direct' AS strategy, '503 after 5.021s' AS http_result, 'orders 0 / outbox 0 / processed 0' AS immediate_db UNION ALL SELECT 2, 'Outbox', '201 after 9.328ms', 'orders 1 / pending outbox 1 / processed 0'

query.description: Reproduces waiting-room outcome, latency, and load medians from the six final 0e9dcb1 summaries.
query.sql: SELECT 'Direct' AS strategy, 'acceptance_share' AS metric, 0.727357 AS value UNION ALL SELECT 'Queued', 'acceptance_share', 1.0 UNION ALL SELECT 'Direct', 'p50_e2e_ms', 52.0 UNION ALL SELECT 'Queued', 'p50_e2e_ms', 14054.5 UNION ALL SELECT 'Direct', 'p95_e2e_ms', 60.0 UNION ALL SELECT 'Queued', 'p95_e2e_ms', 27880.8 UNION ALL SELECT 'Direct', 'p99_e2e_ms', 61.0 UNION ALL SELECT 'Queued', 'p99_e2e_ms', 28255.0 UNION ALL SELECT 'Direct', 'http_requests', 7954.0 UNION ALL SELECT 'Queued', 'http_requests', 191071.0
